item.title: NPR's Moscow and Beijing correspondents discuss the reaction to U.S. elections abroad
item.description: The results of the U.S. midterms were closely followed overseas. NPR correspondents in Moscow and Beijing discuss how the elections are seen in the countries they cover.
item.content:encoded: The results of the U.S. midterms were closely followed overseas. NPR correspondents in Moscow and Beijing discuss how the elections are seen in the countries they cover.

item.title: Republican consultant discusses what went wrong and what's next for the GOP
item.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.

item.title: Historically red state legislatures have flipped. Here's what's on their agenda
item.description: Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.
item.content:encoded: Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.

item.title: Week in politics: Democrats plan for the next Congress, Trump's new Chief of Staff
item.description: Democrats plans for the next Congress, where they'll hold significant majorities in both chambers. Meanwhile, President Trump signals his plans by promoting Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff.
item.content:encoded: Democrats plans for the next Congress, where they'll hold significant majorities in both chambers. Meanwhile, President Trump signals his plans by promoting Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff.

item.title: How Gen Z voters helped fuel a blue wave for Democrats
item.description: Republicans made gains with young voters in 2024, but in this year's midterms Americans under 30 issued a strong rebuke of President Trump and his party, voting decisively for Democrats instead.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans made gains with young voters in 2024, but in this year's midterms Americans under 30 issued a strong rebuke of President Trump and his party, voting decisively for Democrats instead.

(Image credit: Chip Somodevilla)

item.title: UFC's Dana White says he will meet with Trump Monday over offer to be White House press secretary
item.description: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White.

item.title: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

item.title: President of The Heritage Foundation looks ahead to the future of the GOP
item.description: Kevin Roberts, the president of the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, talks about the organization's priorities and hopes for the future of the Republican Party and its policies.

item.title: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed under house arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

item.title: How the new Senate majority shifts control over the federal judiciary
item.description: The change in the Senate's majority party means that starting Jan. 3, Democrats will run federal judicial appointments and may continue to until at least 2030.
